title: [Tutorial]
author: whistling_frank
selftext:
I wrote up a [blog post](https://charmed.ai/blog/use-ai-to-generate-a-3d-video-game-character) explaining how to use the tools at Charmed to build a unique animated 3D character. 

[Fig 1. Stylish hero image](https://preview.redd.it/97fas93w70nc1.png?width=800&format=png&auto=webp&s=1796bb276daece58d0c1c6876059634dce69cc86)

The process includes generating a mesh from a text prompt, upscaling and editing textures using a uv-unwrapped material generator, and auto-rigging and retargeting animations. In the end, you can export an FBX file you can continue to edit in Blender or for integration directly into your game engine.  


[Fig 2. A strafing robot captured mid stride](https://preview.redd.it/d14qqtpk80nc1.png?width=800&format=png&auto=webp&s=9b5267c79d499653a25e1b09a1d4f2b171cc1ac1)

My goal is to make it as fast as possible to get new ideas for 3D games into a playable state. The more ideas we get to try out, the more likely it is to find something fun and worth investing in.  


You can check out the finished [strafing robot](https://hub.charmed.ai/shared-resource/re_2cxvawidMQDUZjKdvOUJI8NINSz) here. Apologies for the forced account creation to see the example- we've got our best team of elves (think Santa, not Tolkein) working on it.
